newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks follow Wall St, close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks follow Wall St, close sharply higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday following the recovery on Wall Street and brokers said the market had more upside before it closed for the handover festivities next week.
The Hang Seng Index closed 174.06 points, or 1.17 percent, higher at 15,065.02 after storming to a high of 15,200.96 in the morning session.
"The market has moved up a lot today on the back of the U.S. rally," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
"It could move up a bit higher, maybe 100 points or so, but after the break I doubt we will see much of an advance after the handover."
Turnover climbed to a very heavy HK$22.72 billion, well above Tuesday's HK$17.37 billion.
The Dow Industrials rebounded overnight by 153.80 points, or 2.02 percent, to 7,758.06, recovering from a 192-point drop the previous day, its largest decline of the year.
The Hong Kong stock exchange will be closed on June 28 through June 2 to mark the territory's return to Chinese rule on July 1. Normal trading will resume on July 3.
Brokers said there was rotational buying in all blue-chip sectors, with the commercial and industrial sector leading over the day.
"There is still value in the blue chips," said James Robertson, vice president at Salomon Brothers.
Conglomerates Swire Pacific put on HK$0.50 to HK$70.25 and CITIC Pacific added HK$0.50 to HK$48.20.

Banking giant HSBC Holdings, the day's most active issue, leaped HK$7.00 to an all-time high of HK$236.00 before easing to close HK$5.00 higher at HK$233.00 on trade of HK$1.01 billion. The bank denied rumours it was interested in acquiring the Royal Bank of Scotland.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index for red chips substantially outperformed the blue chip index but brokers said only selected issues rose.
Shanghai Industrial added HK$1.20 to HK$44.00 and China Resources gained HK$2.05 to HK$31.90.
H-share Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical, offered at HK$1.76, debuted at HK$1.70 then fell further to end at HK$1.64.
Fairform also debuted on Wednesday. It opened at HK$1.32 compared with the offer price of HK$1.08 then rose to close the day at HK$1.49 on moderate trade of HK$71 million.
